sentences: Don't try to win an argument with visions, entities, memories, or cosmic conclusions.
Reflect the feeling and redirect toward safety, non-harm, sleep, and ordinary reality.
Don't tell somebody they are crazy, broken, weak, punished, or failing the medicine.
Don't force eye contact, touch, music, prayer, chanting, interpretation, confession, or insight.

codex: The repeated “Don't” openings and accumulating lists create a uniform, instructional cadence that could suggest AI polishing. Those features also occur in human-written guidance, so they cannot establish authorship.
haiku: All three opening lines begin with "Don't" and each one resolves into a list, so the rhythm is even enough to read as a rule set built to a template. The voice stays impersonal, with no "I," no case, and no particular person, which is how a polished model answer usually sounds.
sonnet: Every sentence is a bare imperative built the same way, mostly "Don't" plus a list of four to eight items, with no example, no person and no explanation. The even, clipped, checklist rhythm and the impersonal voice make it read like generated guidance.
